While in Lyon in summer 2025, I recorded bicycle rides with a GoPro and used the footage's GPS data to reconstruct the routes and turn them into an interactive map.

The project was a simple way to connect something I was already doing — riding around the city — with location data and interactive mapping.

## How I made it

The basic workflow was:

1. Record rides around Lyon with a GoPro.
2. Extract the GPS coordinates associated with the footage.
3. Organize the location data into usable routes.
4. Load the routes into Google My Maps to create an interactive view of where I had ridden.

## Why I like this project

This was a small project, but it made location data feel tangible. Instead of starting with a downloaded dataset, the data came from something I had physically done and recorded myself.

It also gave me a practical introduction to turning raw geographic coordinates into something another person could explore visually.

:::
